name: Caro-Kann Defence (Classical)
summary: Solid pawn structure, the light-squared bishop developed before ...e6, and endgames you can play all day.

notes.8: Bf5 is the point of the Caro-Kann: the bishop gets out before ...e6 closes it in.
notes.12: ...h6 stops h5 trapping the bishop and gives it the h7 square.
notes.14: ...Nd7 first, so that Nf3-e5 can be met by ...Nxe5. ...Ngf6 comes next.
notes.18: The bishops come off; Black has no bad bishop left and a very solid structure.
notes.24: ...Be7 and ...O-O follow. Plans: ...c5 to hit d4, or ...Qa5 and ...O-O-O for a quiet endgame.

notes.6: Against the Advance the bishop still comes out first; ...e6 behind it keeps the structure healthy.
notes.10: ...c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain. Do it before White gets c3 and b4 in.
notes.14: ...Ne7 heads for c6 (or g6/f5). The knight on d7 keeps an eye on e5.
notes.20: ...Be7 and ...O-O; the typical plan is ...f6 to undermine e5, or ...Qb6 against b2 and d4.

notes.8: ...Nc6 develops with a hit on d4 and keeps ...Bg4 in reserve against Nf3.
notes.12: ...Bg4 stops Nf3 for now; the bishop is active before ...e6.
notes.14: Qb3 hits b7 and d5; ...Qd7 covers both calmly (not ...Qb6, which allows Qxb6 and a worse ending).
notes.18: ...Bd6 trades the strong f4 bishop. The structure is symmetric; Black plays ...O-O, ...Rfe8 and a minority attack with ...b5-b4 later.
